text: Far more convincing than Mr. Inglethorp’s stony denials!” I could not help laughing. “My dear Poirot, I am sure you are capable of thinking of seventy! But, seriously, in spite of what I heard you say to the detectives, you surely cannot still believe in the possibility of Alfred Inglethorp’s innocence?” “Why not now as much as before? Nothing has changed.” “But the evidence is so conclusive.” “Yes, too conclusive.” We turned in at the gate of Leastways Cottage, and proceeded up the now familiar stairs. “Yes, yes, too conclusive,” continued Poirot, almost to himself.
